summary: Evening 5xx surge: API gateway backlog + autoscaler slow-warm causing upstream runtime crashloop
description:
Issue summary:
Between 18:05-19:40 UTC on 2026-03-10 we observed a sustained spike in 5xx responses for a subset of ClearMind AI traffic on prod/us-east-1. Symptoms: rapid rise in API gateway 502/503/504 rates, long accept-queue length, followed by upstream serving-runtime processes entering a watchdog restart loop and GPU-related worker evictions.

Impact:
- Customer ClearMind AI (dedicated) reported ~35% error rate on chat and embedding routes; multiple streaming sessions terminated.
- Platform-wide latency tail increased for the us-east-1 partition; some other tenants experienced transient elevated latency but not sustained 5xx.

Initial hypothesis:
Autoscaler slow warm-up + accept-queue backlog caused amplification: API gateway queued requests, proxy replay/hedged retries increased fanout to runtimes that were still cold. Prefetch/kv-cache contention + heavy embedding uploads caused runtimes to hit a watchdog threshold (long GPU stalls) and restart, causing upstream 5xx amplification.

Context / why this is unusual:
We have seen 5xx waves before, but this event correlates strongly with a rapid ephemeral scale-up path where warm workers were delayed by quota throttling and NVMe checkpoint I/O spikes. The serving-runtime responded by evicting tasks (watchdog) rather than graceful shedding, producing runtime crashloop and persistent 502/503 errors at the gateway.

Full incident notes and timeline are below.
steps_to_reproduce: From prod-us-east-1: Run simultaneous workload: continuous embedding upload (5000 small vectors/min) + 250 concurrent short chat streaming sessions to chat-3b-opt for 20 minutes.
Set a temporary autoscaler quota / slow warm path to simulate resource provisioning delay (reduce warm pool growth to 30% of normal for a 5-minute window).
Observe accept-queue depth in api-gateway, worker prefetch latencies, and serving-runtime watchdog logs for GPU stall thresholds.
logs: 2026-03-10T18:07:01Z autoscaler[controller] INFO scale_event=requested=18 provisioned=6 reason=quota-throttle wait=120s
2026-03-10T18:08:45Z runtime[worker-3] ERROR watchdog: gpu_stall=12.8s -> evicting task id=xx34; initiating process-restart
investigation_notes: Checked autoscaler logs: multiple scale requests were queued; cloud quota API returned 429 for instance creation between 18:06-18:10 UTC.
Serving-runtime logs show repeated watchdog-triggered process restarts with stack traces pointing to long GPU kernel stalls (nvml timeout observed intermittently).
NVMe iowait spikes correlated with background snapshotting of embedding shard at 18:04-18:09 — this increased prefetch latency and caused request processing backlog.
API gateway metrics show hedged retries increased 8x as accept_queue > 500; gateway retries contributed to runtime fanout amplification.
We reproduced a smaller-scale version in staging by throttling warm pool growth; results matched production behaviour (accept queue growth -> runtime eviction).
comments: 2026-03-10 18:22 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Applied emergency rate limit on ClearMind AI project to 60r/s for embed/chat routes. This reduced incoming fanout; observed gateway accept_queue drop to ~120 within 3 minutes.

2026-03-10 18:35 - Jillian Kim (Eng - runtime): Noted nvml timeout logs on runtime-3. Launching rolling restart of the 3 affected runtime instances to clear GPU state; collecting core dumps for further analysis.
2026-03-10 19:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer notified of temporary limit and suggested fallback to a lower concurrency profile; customer accepted and implemented client-side backoff.
2026-03-11 09:10 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Adjusted autoscaler warmup thresholds (reduce aggressive scale steps) and increased prewarm pool by 2 instances for us-east-1; monitoring for recurrence.

2026-03-12 11:02 - Runtime team: Deployed hotfix to runtime to delay watchdog eviction threshold by 30% and add a soft-shed path to return 429/503 gracefully before process restart. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
mitigation_and_workaround: Temporary actions applied: (1) Emergency per-tenant rate limit for ClearMind AI on embed/chat routes; (2) Rolling restart of affected runtime workers to clear GPU/NVML state; (3) Increase prewarm pool for us-east-1 to reduce cold starts; (4) Customer-side backoff recommended. These reduced 5xx rate from ~35% to <2% for the impacted routes within ~25 minutes.
action_items: SRE: Work with cloud provider to remove transient quota throttling and investigate instance creation latency (owner: Marco Ruiz).
Runtime: Analyze core dumps and GPU driver traces to determine root cause of nvml timeouts (owner: Jillian Kim).
Autoscaler: Add a better backpressure signal from api-gateway accept-queue to the scaler to avoid scale amplification (owner: Priya Desai).
Product/Platform: Add route-level automatic graceful-shed path to return 429 when accept_queue exceeds configurable threshold (owner: Tom Nguyen).
resolution: Work in progress. Immediate customer impact mitigated with temporary rate limits and prewarm increase. Hotfix to graceful-shed behavior merged and scheduled for canary rollout (us-east-1) on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. Awaiting deeper analysis of NVML timeouts and cloud quota events for permanent root cause. Pending follow-ups tracked in action_items.
